channel.title: The Jukebug
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The Jukebug" - What if that song you got stuck in your head stayed there?

item.title: Re: It just doesn't feel, "SCP" enough.
item.content:encoded:
Oh No! When editing I took out the lines where I explained what I meant by "encourages you to act on your intrusive thoughts!" So, intrusive thoughts are thoughts that you have impulsively. More often than not these thoughts are violent. People who have been affected by this "magic earworm" have committed acts from strange but harmless behavior all the way up to homicide and self-mutilation. This was actually inspired by something that happened to me the other day. I was cooking and chopping onions and I was singing a song in my head, when an intrusive thought popped up and said "chop your finger off." I started singing "chop your finger off" to the tune of the song that was stuck in my head. I feel so dumb for leaving out the explanation. I was erasing fluff lines to stay under the word count but I must have erased the wrong ones.

Also, I'm glad you asked about if it can appear randomly. Yes it absolutely can. That is how the phenomenon starts in Patient 0, seemingly at random. The Foundation has contained at least a dozen outbreaks in the past, all in different areas around the world. Usually, these outbreaks are 5-10 years apart from each other and leads credence to the "phenomenon theory." However, the past three outbreaks have all been within the past three years. The staff that believes in the "entity theory "believes the entity is going through a sort of molting period, they believe that this entity feeds on sanity and is about to evolve. So it requires more sustenance and is moving at a much faster rate. In the original findings, people who had the "Jukebug" could not transmit it through recordings, and it was safe to record any singing the afflicted did. However within the past three years, the "Jukebug" phenomenon or entity has evolved to be able to spread through audio and visual recording, so the Foundation has revoked clearance for recording.

I know it seems like a lot I left out in the pitch, however I wanted the basics explained first, which I apparently failed to do. Thank you for your input and for taking the time to read this.

item.title: It just doesn't feel, "SCP" enough.
item.content:encoded: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to say it has to be dangerous, it just, it feels like a magic earworm. Also, I don't think it's an audio cognitohazard (keep in mind cognitohazards are probably my weakest point in foundation cannon, so don't take my word for it) Also, can it appear in your brain randomly, or was everyone infected, infected by a patient 0 or someone who interacted with patient 0.

item.title: The Jukebug
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Page Format: I plan to use the standard page format, adding in interviews and audio logs to tell the stories of three separate cases.

Elevator Pitch: An auditory cognitohazard that latches onto the brain waves of a person until the afflicted person hears a “catchy" song. Once the afflicted has a song stuck in their head, the anomaly perverts the lyrics to encourage the afflicted to act out intrusive thoughts. The anomaly can lie dormant for up to three days without a song to embed itself into, before eventually dissipating. The anomaly can be detected through basic brain activity scans, appearing in the shape of an insect on images of the brain. If a song is introduced that the afflicted finds catchy, the anomaly will stay undetected by the afflicted for two more days. During which it will play the song excessively in their mind. Anytime the afflicted sings the song, their brainwaves are modified to transmit the anomaly into the minds of others, starting a separate cycle. After the two day infection period, the anomaly begins to goad the original afflicted. The more the afflicted resists, the harder it pushes with symptoms ranging in severity. The Foundation can eradicate the anomalous brain activity by playing music that lacks (in the opinion of the listener) pleasant rhythm or rhyme, for 18 hours.

It is unclear if this anomaly is merely a phenomenon or an entity. No evidence of an entity occupying the physical body of any afflicted people exist, other than vivid descriptions of a singing insect-like creature seen during the REM cycles of the afflicted, in the first several days of exposure. The vivid and consistent descriptions of this creature, coupled with the insect-shaped brain image, have lead to a dichotomy in the observing staff. Those who believe it is merely a phenomenon, which the evidence seems to support the most, have developed the current SCP protocols. A separate team, continues to search for evidence of what they call the “Jukebug.”
Central Narrative: Multiple accounts of different instances of the “Jukebug,” including: the aftermath of a child's birthday party, a surgeon, and a musician working on their newest song.

Hook: I think the idea that you could have been infected by this SCP and it’s already too late is spine-chilling and compelling enough to draw people in.

Additional Notes: Since the anomaly spreads due to divergent brainwaves of a person during the recitation of the song in their mind I am not sure if this is actually an auditory cognitohazard or not.
